correctness.rationale: The exact independent-Poisson model gives product and sum objective identities; both are strictly concave in their relevant coordinates. Negative derivative at A-only excludes that endpoint. Rational polynomial identities yield exactly two gates per objective and exact equality cases; monotonicity of an exponential ratio gives the sharp two-target obstruction. verify.py recomputes identities over fractions and checks 64,800 finite comparisons, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with How 2024 (multiple primers and sampling volume), Baetscher 2023 (greedy empirical portfolio), and Fukaya 2022 (Bayesian expected-richness depth/replicates) finds none proving the same exact combined product-vs-sum allocation result. Current mathematical records and accessible own-claim history were checked for the exact two opposite windows and sharp three-taxon reentry; adjacent results optimize different objectives or a specialist-only assay. Priority remains provisional with residual wider optimization-literature risk.
residual_risks: General reliability and experimental-design literature might contain equivalent abstract examples not identified by semantic search.

value.rationale: Studies of heterogeneous primer sensitivity and eDNA budget optimization motivate the distinction between detecting every priority taxon and maximizing mean taxon count. The constructed three-target case proves two separated, opposite budget-allocation disagreements with no assay fully blind to any taxon, plus a sharp minimum of three targets for all-target reentry. These are precise decisions not implied by expected-richness-only optimization; quantitative gains are not claimed to apply to measured primers.
